label: models/fw_drum.mdl: a rusted 55-gallon drum with a hazard stripe

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/testsphere.mdl, models/gib_legbone.mdl, models/big_rock.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: The outline is a plain rectangle in the four side views and a square from above and below. A 55-gallon drum is round in plan, so its top and bottom outlines are wrong. It is a box, not a drum, and the brief's drum outline is missing.

M2.reason: Measured size is 23 x 23 x 34, exactly the brief's 34 high and 23 across (sizeOff 0). Within 10%.

M3.reason: The drum's parts are missing: no rim or chime bands, no lid or bung, no seam. Only one solid block is there.

M4.reason: A single flat mid-grey throughout. The brief asks for a rusted steel drum, and no rust colouring or metal variation shows in any view or in the line-up. Colour is present but clearly off.

M5.reason: The hazard stripe the brief names is missing, and so is any rust or wear. The faces show only a faint noise texture, with no markings.

M6.reason: In the line-up it is the plain grey box (B). Beside the testsphere, the bone and the rock, a player would not take it for one of Half-Life's props. It reads as a placeholder block.

M7.reason: It stands upright with its tall axis vertical, which is the drum's pose. Front and facing cannot be told apart on a box, and the origin's placement cannot be verified from the pictures. Not a must-have item.

M8.reason: The SMAK check reports no errors. At 12 triangles it is under twice the Half-Life median of 62 (the limit is 124). The box is closed, with nothing open, inside out or floating.
